chunks: Al-Ḥusayn ibn Abī al-ʿAlāʾ asked him about a garment for the muhrim that saffron affects, then it is washed, so he said:
"There is no harm in it if its scent has gone. Even if it had been entirely dyed, if it has shifted toward whiteness and been washed, then there is no harm."

key_terms.الثَّوْبِ: a garment or piece of clothing
key_terms.الزَّعْفَرَانُ: saffron, whose scent or dye affects the ruling here
key_terms.الْبَيَاضِ: whiteness, indicating the fading of the dye’s effect
key_terms.الْمُحْرِمِ: a person in the state of ihram

ai.seo_question: Can a muhrim wear a garment that was stained or dyed with saffron after washing it?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning what a muhrim may wear during ihram when a garment has been affected by saffron. It states that if the scent is removed and the garment is washed, there is no problem in wearing it, even if it had been fully dyed so long as it has become inclined toward whiteness.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2607 - Al-Husayn ibn Abi al-‘Ala’ asked Imam (as) about a garment for a Muhrim that has been stained with saffron and then washed.
Imam (as) said: "There is no harm in it if the scent has been removed. Even if it has been entirely dyed, as long as it leans toward whiteness and has been washed, there is no harm in it."
